featured_reviews.name: Mansoor Kanchwala
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Old Church: The foundation of the original St Peter’s Church was laid in April 12, 1852, by Bishop Hartmann. The Church was completed in September 1853. It measured approximately 100 by 75 feet. In 1867 a second storey was added to the old top floor.
The storey above the Church was at first used as the priests’ residence and parish school. In 1855, the Jesuit Seminary was transferred from Surat to Bandra, and the seminary and the parish schools were merged. In 1863, the seminary was again transferred to Bombay, and the Boys’ Orphanage from Bombay came to Bandra. This was the beginning of the St Stanislaus’ High School.

The New Church: As far back as August 1887, the then Archbishop of Bombay issued the following appeal: “The poor parish of St. Peter’s Bandora, numbers with the orphans (boys and girls) 2215 souls and has for a church the floor of the boys’ Orphanage. This place is much too small and is ill-suited for divine service. A new and more spacious Church is much needed and will be a great benefit to the poor Parishioners and the Orphans”.

The growing needs of the parish necessitated the building of a larger Church, and so in September, 1938, Archbishop Thomas Roberts, S.J. blessed the foundation stone of the present St Peter’s Church.

The new Church has been built on the site of the old and has been designed on the Romanesque style, this is one of the best example of awesome architecture! Every where you see in this church will leave you awestruck! You'll be confused to decide what and where to see! The alter is pretty basic but holds a significant meaning! The statue of Risen Christ immediately makes you feel like home!
It is easily accessible from Bandra station! One can walk for 15 min to reach here or taken an sharing auto or the best BEST BUS (211, 214, 219 all AC charging just 6/-).
If you're visiting mount mary add this church in your must visit church list!

Mass timings:
Morning not sure
Evening (mon to fri: 7:00)
Saturday: 7:30 (sunday mass)
All in English.

featured_reviews.name: Joseph Nunes
featured_reviews.review_text:
St. Andrew’s Church, with its 400+ years of rich history, has recently undergone a transformative 20-month renovation that beautifully preserves its heritage while rejuvenating its spiritual ambiance.

✨ Architectural Revival
Façade and Roof Rejuvenation: Heritage specialists like Jivraj Sankhat and Savani Heritage Conservation expertly restored the church’s iconic roof, façade, marble, woodwork, and stained-glass windows, reviving their original splendor.

Traditional Techniques: The renovation prioritized authenticity. Over 5.5 ft thick walls were replastered with lime instead of cement—an effort to maintain the church’s historical integrity.

🌞 Rediscovered Beauty
Choir Loft & Lighting: Long-hidden architectural gems, such as the choir loft’s clerestory windows, were uncovered—reintroducing natural light into the nave and restoring a key visual element of the original design.

💒 Interior Elegance
Faithfully Restored Altars: The Portuguese-inspired altars, once scarred by moisture and termite damage, were carefully conserved and revived to their former glory.

Wooden Pulpit Revival: Carved with biblical narrative, the original pulpit was meticulously restored, complete with its ornate canopy—allowing worshippers to once more feel its spiritual resonance.

⏳ Heritage Sensitivity & Community Effort
Meticulous, Not Hasty: From April 2024 to December 2025, the renovation focused on preservation over superficial repairs—respecting the church’s Portuguese colonial architecture.

Community-Driven, Funded by Love: Entirely financed by parishioners and diaspora support, the project faced financial hurdles—yet the community’s unwavering commitment ensured the work reached its homestretch.

🎖 A Joyous Reopening
On a beautiful Sunday evening, over a thousand worshippers celebrated the church’s rededication—blessed by Cardinal Oswald Gracias—marking a poignant return to its rightful spiritual grandeur.

In summary, the recent renovations at St. Andrew’s Church masterfully balance respect for its centuries-old heritage with modern integrity. From the reimagined façade to the restored interior treasures, every detail reflects love, care, and unwavering faith. It’s a testament to what can be achieved when a community unites to preserve its legacy—and a spiritually uplifting sanctuary reborn.

featured_reviews.name: Sean Kennedy
featured_reviews.review_text:
St Vincent De Paul Church is more than a place of worship—it is a layered story of faith, time, and community, expressed through five defining pillars:

Miracles
Stories of quiet grace echo through generations—answered prayers, moments of healing, and an unspoken belief that faith here finds its way. The church carries an aura where the intangible feels deeply personal.

Heritage
Rooted in the legacy of Chuim village, its origins date back to the 1940s, evolving alongside Mumbai’s transformation while preserving its old-world soul and spiritual continuity.

Architecture
A harmonious blend of simplicity and purpose, its structure balances modern functionality with sacred calm—featuring serene interiors, soft natural light, and spaces designed for reflection.

Parishioners
The heartbeat of the church—diverse yet deeply connected. Generations of families shape its identity, carrying forward traditions with warmth, service, and collective faith.

Activities
Beyond prayer, it thrives as a hub of engagement—community outreach, youth initiatives, charitable work, and celebrations that bind people together in purpose and spirit.

featured_reviews.name: Yash Shah
featured_reviews.review_text: Girgaon, formerly Girgaum, is an area in southern Mumbai in Maharashtra, India. Charni Road railway station serves Girgaon. The culture in Girgaon is diverse and varied. Like most areas of cosmopolitan Mumbai, residents span diverse languages, religions, traditions, festivals, and attire. Girgaon occupies prime residential real estate due to increasing demand just because of its prominent location in South Mumbai. The Sanskrit term "Giri" stands for hills, whereas the Sanskrit word "gram" denotes a village. Thus, Girgaon means a village at the foothill of mountains. A birds' eye view from the top of Malabar Hill will justify this etymological finding.

featured_reviews.name: StayEatReview
featured_reviews.review_text:
Stepping into Emmanuel Church feels like walking through a quiet chapter of history preserved in stone. The beautiful black-stone architecture, arched wooden doors, and vintage stained-glass windows create a peaceful and spiritual atmosphere that instantly slows you down from the busy city pace.

What truly stands out is the heritage charm inside the church. The old memorial plaques, handcrafted marble pulpit, and colorful circular stained-glass artwork reflect timeless craftsmanship and deep historical significance. Every corner tells a story from another era, making it a wonderful place for history lovers, architecture enthusiasts, and photography seekers.

A hidden heritage gem in Mumbai that deserves more attention for its architecture, history, and spiritual calmness.
